meta.titre: Climatic Zones of Cameroon: equatorial, coastal, Sudan, Sahelian and highland types compared
meta.sous_theme: Climatic types of Cameroon, their location, rainfall, temperature, vegetation and causes

sections.contenu_markdown: Imagine a long journey by road from Douala to Maroua. You start in warm, wet country with thick forest, climb to cooler grassland, and finish in a hot, dry land of thorny bushes where the rains are short and uncertain. Cameroon's climate changes completely along that single journey. Geography papers ask you to name the climatic types, to place them on an outline map of Cameroon and to describe each one. If you know the five zones in order from south to north, with the highland as a special case, these questions are easy.

items: Climate is the average weather of a place over many years, measured by rainfall and temperature.
Rainfall is measured in millimetres and temperature in degrees Celsius.
Places near the equator are hot all year, and temperature falls as height above sea level increases.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Why Cameroon has several climates
- **Latitude.** Cameroon stretches from about 2° N to about 13° N, so the length of the rainy season shortens as you go north.
- **Winds.** Moist south-westerly winds from the Atlantic bring the rains. The dry, dusty harmattan from the Sahara brings the dry season.
- **Relief.** Height lowers temperature, and mountains cause relief rainfall on their windward slopes.

| Zone | Where | Rainfall | Temperature | Vegetation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Equatorial (Guinean type) | Southern plateau | Heavy, two rainy and two dry seasons | Hot, small range | Dense equatorial forest |
| Cameroon (coastal) type | Coast, slopes of Mount Cameroon | Very heavy, one long rainy season | Hot, humid, very small range | Mangrove and rainforest |
| Sudan type | Adamawa plateau, Benue lowlands | Moderate, one rainy and one long dry season | Hot, larger range | Tall-grass savanna |
| Sahelian | Far North | Low, short, unreliable | Very hot, large range | Thorn scrub, short grass |
| Highland | West and North-West | Heavy, one long rainy season | Cool because of height | Montane forest and grassland |

### Soils linked to the zones
Red, leached **ferralitic** soils lie under the forest. Fertile **volcanic** soils occur around Mount Cameroon and in parts of the highlands. **Ferruginous** soils are typical of the savanna, and thin sandy soils occur in the far north.

### Effects on farming
Forest zones grow cocoa, oil palm, plantains and cassava; the Sudan savanna grows cotton, sorghum and millet and supports cattle; the highlands grow arabica coffee and vegetables.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question gives monthly rainfall and temperature
variantes.contenu_markdown: Add the monthly rainfall for the annual total, count the rainy peaks and the dry months, and find the temperature range (hottest month minus coolest month). Two peaks and small range point to the equatorial type; one peak and a long dry season point to the Sudan type; low total with a short season points to the Sahel.

variantes.nom: Locating zones on an outline map
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says locate and name on the outline map
variantes.contenu_markdown: Draw a short label inside the zone, not outside it, and work from south to north: forest, Adamawa, north. Mark the **economic capital Douala** on the coast and the **political capital Yaounde** on the southern plateau. Industrial zones include Douala, Yaounde, Edea and Limbe. Name every item that is asked.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to describe or compare the climate
variantes.contenu_markdown: Cover **location, rainfall (total and pattern), temperature (average and range), vegetation**. For a comparison, write one sentence per feature that contrasts the two zones, for example *Douala has one long rainy season while Maroua has a short unreliable one*.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A weather station records the following monthly rainfall in millimetres, from January to December: 40, 70, 160, 190, 220, 150, 70, 80, 210, 270, 110, 30. The warmest month has an average of 27°C and the coolest month 24°C.
(a) Calculate the total annual rainfall and the temperature range.
(b) Describe the pattern of the rainy seasons.
(c) Name the climatic zone and the natural vegetation.

etapes.action: Add all twelve monthly figures for part (a).
etapes.justification: The annual total is the sum of the monthly rainfall.

etapes.action: Subtract the coolest month from the warmest month.
etapes.justification: The temperature range shows whether the climate is even or varied.

etapes.action: Look for the peaks in the rainfall figures for part (b).
etapes.justification: The month with the largest rainfall marks the middle of a rainy season.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Peaks in May (220 mm) and October (270 mm), with a lower trough in July and August (70 mm and 80 mm).

etapes.action: Match the data with a zone for part (c).
etapes.justification: Heavy rain, two peaks and a very small range are the features of the Guinean equatorial type.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Equatorial (Guinean) type, with dense equatorial forest.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) **1,600 mm** of rain a year; temperature range **3°C**. (b) There are two rainy seasons, with peaks in May and October, separated by a dip in July and August. (c) The station lies in the **equatorial zone (Guinean type)** and the natural vegetation is **dense equatorial forest**.

items.erreur_markdown: "Cameroon has only an equatorial climate because it is near the equator."
items.pourquoi_faux: Cameroon extends over about eleven degrees of latitude and has mountains and a coast, so it has five types of climate.
items.correction_markdown: Name the **equatorial, coastal, Sudan, Sahelian and highland** types and place them.

items.erreur_markdown: Placing the Sahelian climate in the south and the equatorial climate in the north.
items.pourquoi_faux: Rainfall decreases from south to north. The south is wet and forested; the far north is dry.
items.correction_markdown: **Equatorial in the south; Sudan in the middle; Sahelian in the Far North.**

items.pourquoi_faux: The harmattan is a dry, dusty wind from the Sahara. The rains come with moist south-westerly winds from the Atlantic.
items.correction_markdown: **Harmattan = dry season; south-west winds = rainy season.**

items.erreur_markdown: "Highland areas of Cameroon are hot because the country is close to the equator."
items.pourquoi_faux: Temperature falls with height, by about 6.5°C for every 1,000 m, so the highlands are cool.
items.correction_markdown: The highlands are **cooler because of height above sea level**.

items.erreur_markdown: Naming a zone without saying where it is when the question says locate and name.
items.pourquoi_faux: Both the position and the name are needed to earn the mark.
items.correction_markdown: *The Sahelian zone lies in the Far North, near Lake Chad.*

items.enonce_markdown: Match each type of vegetation to its climatic zone: (1) tall-grass savanna, (2) thorn scrub and short grass, (3) dense equatorial forest, (4) montane grassland. The zones are Sudan, Sahelian, Equatorial and Highland.
items.solution_markdown: (1) tall-grass savanna: **Sudan**. (2) thorn scrub and short grass: **Sahelian**. (3) dense equatorial forest: **Equatorial**. (4) montane grassland: **Highland**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A town records these monthly rainfall figures in millimetres from January to December: 0, 0, 20, 70, 120, 160, 230, 280, 210, 90, 5, 0. Take a month with less than 30 mm as a dry month.
(a) Calculate the annual total.
(b) State the number of dry months and the month with most rain.
(c) Name the climatic zone and give a reason.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $0 + 0 + 20 + 70 + 120 + 160 + 230 + 280 + 210 + 90 + 5 + 0 = 1\,185$ mm. The total is **1,185 mm**.
(b) The dry months are January, February, March, November and December: **5 dry months**. August has the most rain, **280 mm**.
(c) The zone is the **Sudan type**, because there is one rainy season with a single peak and a long dry season.

items.enonce_markdown:
A town at sea level in the south has an average temperature of 26°C. A second town lies at 1,600 m in the highlands. Take the fall in temperature to be 6.5°C for every 1,000 m.
(a) Calculate the temperature expected at the highland town.
(b) Explain why the slopes of Mount Cameroon facing the Atlantic receive very heavy rainfall.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Fall $= 1.6 \times 6.5 = 10.4^\circ$C. Temperature $= 26 - 10.4 = 15.6^\circ$C. The highland town has about **15.6°C**.
(b) Moist south-westerly winds blow from the Atlantic onto the mountain. The air is forced to rise, cools, and condenses into cloud, and heavy **relief rainfall** falls on the windward slopes. This is why the coastal zone near the mountain is among the wettest in Africa.

items_markdown: Cameroon has five climatic types: equatorial (Guinean), coastal (Cameroon type), Sudan, Sahelian and highland.
Rainfall falls from south to north: dense forest in the south, savanna in the middle, thorn scrub in the Far North.
Moist south-westerly winds bring the rains; the dry harmattan from the Sahara brings the dry season.
Temperature drops about 6.5°C for every 1,000 m, so the highlands are cool.
To describe a climate cover location, rainfall, temperature and vegetation; to identify it from data, find the total, the peaks and the range.
On an outline map, label each zone inside its area, and mark Douala (economic capital) and Yaounde (political capital).
